name: Waist circumference
rangeNote: Above 94 cm (men) or 80 cm (women) is linked to higher heart and metabolic risk in people of European descent; for South and East Asian people the limits are lower (90 and 80 cm). Measure standing, breathing out gently, halfway between the lowest rib and the top of the hip bone.
summary: Waist size shows fat around the belly, which is more closely linked to heart and metabolic risk than weight alone. Your waist divided by your height (waist-to-height ratio) works for everyone: below 0.5 is the usual guide.

high.meaning: A larger waist is linked to higher blood pressure, blood sugar and blood fats, and to heart disease, even at the same weight.

low.meaning: There's no lower limit for waist size; a small waist on its own isn't a problem.
